sections.title: What This Module Covers
sections.body: This module covers the Rails framework architecture at the foundational level that every fresher interview starts with. You will learn the Model-View-Controller pattern and how each layer has a single responsibility, Rails' opinionated directory structure and what lives where (app/models, app/controllers, app/views, config/routes.rb, db/), routing from the router to the controller action, controller basics including the params hash, instance variables shared with views, before_action filters, and the difference between render and redirect_to, the ERB view layer and how it renders HTML, and layouts and partials for DRY templates.

sections.title: Key Concepts at a Glance
sections.body: MVC: Model handles data and business logic, View renders the UI, Controller receives requests and coordinates. Rails directory: app/ has models, controllers, views, helpers, mailers, jobs, channels. config/routes.rb defines URL-to-action mappings. db/ has migrations and schema.rb. Gemfile lists dependencies. resources :posts generates 7 RESTful routes (index, show, new, create, edit, update, destroy). params hash contains URL parameters, query strings, and form data. Controller instance variables (@post) are automatically available in views. before_action :method_name runs before specified actions. render :template_name renders without redirect. redirect_to url sends a 302 and the browser makes a new request — use after creating/updating/deleting. ERB: <%= %> outputs, <% %> executes, <%# %> comments. Partials: _partial_name.html.erb, rendered with render 'partial_name'. Layouts in app/views/layouts/application.html.erb wrap all views.

sections.title: What Interviewers Ask Freshers
sections.body: Most common Rails MVC fresher questions: (1) Explain the MVC pattern and how Rails implements it. (2) What happens when a user visits a URL in a Rails app? Walk through the request lifecycle. (3) What routes does resources :posts generate? (4) What is the difference between render and redirect_to? (5) What is the params hash and what does it contain? (6) What is a before_action and why is it useful? (7) What is the purpose of the application layout? (8) What is a partial and when would you use one? (9) Where do you define routes in Rails? (10) What does Convention over Configuration mean in Rails? These questions test whether you understand Rails as a framework, not just as code you copy-paste.
